mainTopic: Which buildings and gates need a מזוזה. A ברייתא uses the word ״בַּיִת״ to set the limits of the obligation, and that ברייתא refutes רב יהודה. Then רב שמואל בר יהודה teaches a list of gates exempt from מזוזה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that uses the word ״בַּיִת״ to set three limits on מזוזה: a place for living, a place of dignity, and a non-holy place. Because this ברייתא obligates barns and storehouses, רב יהודה is refuted with a תיובתא. Next, רב שמואל בר יהודה recites a list of 'six' gates exempt from מזוזה, and רבא points out that he listed seven. The answer is that the שער המדי (an arched gate) is a dispute between רבי מאיר and חכמים, and אביי explains that they argue over חוקקין להשלים. A new ברייתא then rules that a בית הכנסת, a woman's house and a partners' house need a מזוזה, and the גמרא shows that ״ביתך״ teaches that the מזוזה goes on the right side, following רבא. A parallel ברייתא says the same three houses can get נגעים, and the word ״לו״ is read as a lesson about the stingy owner. Finally, the גמרא resolves a contradiction about whether a בית הכנסת gets נגעים with several answers, and the third answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First limit: only places used for living
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. It says that a gatehouse, a porch and a balcony are excluded from מזוזה because ״בַּיִת״ means a place used for living.
steps.simpleTranslation: [I might think to include even] a gatehouse, a porch and a balcony. So the verse says ״בַּיִת״: just as a house is meant for living in, these are excluded, because they are not meant for living in.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא already included barns and storehouses through ״וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ״. Now it puts a first limit on that inclusion using the word ״בַּיִת״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ״ could seem to include every structure with a gate. ״בַּיִת״ narrows it: the place must be meant for living, the way a house is. A gatehouse, porch and balcony are only passageways or extras, not living spaces, so they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Gatehouse, a small guard room at the entrance to a courtyard
Balcony or corridor leading to several homes
The verse teaches us (introduces the verse that resolves the question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new ברייתא. It is the middle of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד. The words ״יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה״ ("I might include") that come before ״בֵּית שַׁעַר״ appear there.

phrases.english: [I might include] a gatehouse, a portico and a balcony —
phrases.notes: Continues the words 'I might include' from the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: therefore the verse says: "House";
just as a house is designated for living in,
these are excluded, since they are not designated for living in.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בַּיִת״, מָה בַּיִת מְיוּחָד לְדִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד, which was brought as a proof against רב יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that all agree barns and storehouses are exempt from מזוזה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that includes barns through ״וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ״ and limits the inclusion through ״בַּיִת״.

steps.title: Second limit: only places meant for dignity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא excludes a bathroom, a tannery, a bathhouse and a מקוה, because ״בַּיִת״ means a place made for honorable use.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think to include even a bathroom, a tannery, a bathhouse and a מקוה. So the verse says ״בַּיִת״: just as a house is made for dignity, so too anything made for dignity is included. These are excluded, because they are not made for dignity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second limit. A place that people do live in or use still needs to be a dignified place to need a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bathhouse or a tannery is a real building that people spend time in, so the first limit alone might not exclude it. The ברייתא adds a second quality learned from ״בַּיִת״: a house is a respectable place. Places that are dirty or where people undress are not respectable, so they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Tannery, where hides are processed (bad-smelling work)
Made for dignity or honorable use

phrases.english: I might think that I include
even a bathroom and a tannery
and a bathhouse and an immersion house —
therefore the verse says: "House";
just as a house is made for dignity —
so too everything made for dignity [is obligated];
these are excluded, since they are not made for dignity.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit, also learned from ״בַּיִת״, on top of the first limit.

steps.title: Third limit: only non-holy places
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא excludes the הר הבית, the לשכות and the עזרות, because ״בַּיִת״ means an ordinary, non-holy place.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think to include even the הר הבית, its chambers and its courtyards. So the verse says ״בַּיִת״: just as a house is ordinary (non-holy), so too anything ordinary is included. These are excluded, because they are holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its third and last limit. Holy places of the מקדש are excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לשכות of the מקדש are dignified, and some people even stayed in them, so the first two limits would not exclude them. ״בַּיִת״ teaches a third quality: a house is a private, חול place. Places that are קודש are exempt. This is why the topic comes up in מסכת יומא, which discusses the לשכת פרהדרין where the כהן גדול stayed.

keyTerms.meaning: Chambers or rooms in the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This limit connects to the larger discussion in יומא about whether the לשכת פרהדרין needed a מזוזה.

phrases.english: I might think that I include
even the Temple Mount, the chambers and the courtyards —
therefore the verse says: "House";
just as a house is non-sacred —
so too everything non-sacred [is obligated];
these are excluded, since they are sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף הַר הַבַּיִת וְהַלְּשָׁכוֹת וְהָעֲזָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final limit learned from ״בַּיִת״. It completes the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The completed ברייתא, which includes barns and storehouses through ״וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ״.

steps.title: רב יהודה is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that a תנא obligates barns and storehouses in מזוזה, so רב יהודה's claim that everyone exempts them is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation [of רב יהודה].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא decisively refutes רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said there is no opinion that obligates barns and storehouses. This ברייתא does obligate them, through ״וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ״. So רב כהנא is right that it is a מחלוקת תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation of an אמורא's statement

steps.whatToRemember: The word ״בַּיִת״ gives three limits on מזוזה: a place for living, a place of dignity, and a non-holy place. One ברייתא obligates barns and storehouses, so רב יהודה is refuted and רב כהנא's view that this is a מחלוקת stands.

phrases.english: A conclusive refutation.
phrases.notes: This knocks down what רב יהודה said, that everyone agrees barns and storehouses are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the completed ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה is refuted. There is a תנא who obligates barns and storehouses in מזוזה.

steps.title: A list of six gates exempt from מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה recites a ברייתא before רבא: six gates are exempt from מזוזה. He then lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה taught before רבא: Six gates are exempt from מזוזה. They are: a hay storehouse, a cattle barn, a woodshed, a storehouse, a Median gate, a gate without a roof, and a gate not ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about gates that are exempt from מזוזה. It is setting up רבא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא follows the view that barns and storehouses are exempt, the opposite of the ברייתא we just learned. It also adds gates that are exempt because of their shape. A Median gate is an arch with no real doorposts. The other two are a gate with no roof over it and a gate lower than ten טפחים. Count carefully: the list has seven items, not six.

keyTerms.meaning: Median gate, an arched gate without proper doorposts and lintel

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda taught before Rava:
Six gates are exempt from the mezuza:
a hay storehouse, and a cattle barn,
and a woodshed, and a storehouse,
and a Median gate, and a gate that is not roofed,
and a gate that is not ten [handbreadths] high.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion with a different ברייתא listing exempt gates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Barns, storehouses, Median gates, unroofed gates and gates under ten טפחים are exempt from מזוזה.

steps.title: רבא: you said six but listed seven
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the wording: the ברייתא opened by saying six gates, but it listed seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You started with six and ended with seven!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that the number at the start of the list does not match the items listed. The גמרא will need to explain this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא's number is meant to be exact, so a mismatch means something is wrong with the list. Either one item does not belong, or two items are really one case. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: He said to him: You began with six,
and you concluded with seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal count of the ברייתא just recited.
steps.kashyaTarget: The number six stated at the opening of רב שמואל בר יהודה's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list contains seven items, which contradicts the stated count of six.

steps.title: The Median gate is subject to a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the six-versus-seven problem: the שער המדי is disputed by תנאים, so not everyone counts it among the exempt gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the Median gate is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's question about why the ברייתא said 'six' but listed seven. The extra item, the שער המדי, is a matter of dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of 'six' reflects one view, which holds that a שער המדי is not exempt. The listing of seven adds the שער המדי according to the opposing view, which exempts it. So the mismatch is not a mistake. It comes from two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'Median gate', an arched gateway whose top narrows like a dome
It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: The one answering here is רבא himself.

phrases.english: The Median gate is a dispute of Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שַׁעַר הַמָּדִי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the discrepancy to a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא miscounted, saying six but listing seven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The count of six follows one view, and the seventh gate is added according to the other view, which exempts the שער המדי.

steps.title: Proof: רבי מאיר and the Sages argue about a dome-shaped gateway
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר obligates a כיפה (arched gateway) in מזוזה and חכמים exempt it. Both agree that if the straight sides reach ten טפחים, it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a dome-shaped gateway, רבי מאיר obligates it in מזוזה and חכמים exempt it. They agree that if its base (the straight sides) is ten טפחים high, it needs a מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that arched gates really are a dispute between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כיפה is the same kind of gate as the שער המדי: its sides start curving inward instead of going straight up. רבי מאיר still requires a מזוזה, and חכמים do not. If the straight part of the sides is ten טפחים tall, it is a normal doorway, so everyone agrees it needs a מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: At its foot, meaning the straight lower part of the sides

phrases.english: As it was taught: a dome-shaped gateway,
Rabbi Meir obligates it in mezuza,
and the Sages exempt it.
And they agree that if its base has ten handbreadths,
it is obligated in mezuza.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כִּיפָּה, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב בִּמְזוּזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the obligation of an arched gate (שער המדי) is disputed by תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a כיפה: רבי מאיר obligates it and חכמים exempt it

steps.title: אביי: cases where everyone agrees the gate is nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that if the gate is ten טפחים tall but its straight sides are under three, or the sides are three but the gate is under ten tall, everyone agrees it is not a doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: everyone agrees that if it is ten טפחים high but its base is not three, it is nothing. Or if its base is three but it is not ten high, it is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to define the exact case of the dispute by first listing cases that everyone agrees are exempt. This prepares the next step, where he states where they actually argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doorway needs a height of ten טפחים, plus straight sides of at least three טפחים. If either one is missing, it is not considered a doorway at all, according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing (it has no legal status as a doorway)

phrases.english: Abaye said: according to everyone,
if it is ten high and its base is not three —
it is nothing.
Or, if its base is three
but it is not ten high —
it is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute from step 8 by first removing the cases everyone agrees on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gate lacking either ten טפחים of height or three טפחים of straight sides is not a doorway at all.

steps.title: The real dispute: may we imagine carving out the missing width
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר and חכמים argue only when the gate has the height and the sides but is not four טפחים wide, and there is room to carve it wider. רבי מאיר holds חוקקין להשלים, and חכמים hold אין חוקקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only where it is ten high, with a base of three, but not four wide, and there is room to carve it out to complete four. רבי מאיר holds: we carve out to complete. חכמים hold: we do not carve out to complete.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pinpoints the exact case of the dispute and the principle behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gate is too narrow, but the wall beside it could be carved to make it four טפחים wide. רבי מאיר treats the possible carving as if it were already done, so a מזוזה is required. חכמים go only by what actually exists, so the gate is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: We may imagine carving out space to complete a minimum size

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute over arched gates comes down to חוקקין להשלים: does a space that could be carved out count as if it were already there?

phrases.english: They disagreed only where it is ten high
and its base has three
but its width is not four,
and there is room to carve it out to complete four.
Rabbi Meir holds: we carve out to complete.
And the Rabbis hold: we do not carve out to complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's definition by stating the actual case of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר holds חוקקין להשלים, so the gate is obligated. חכמים hold אין חוקקין להשלים, so it is exempt.

steps.title: בית הכנסת, woman's house and partners' house need a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא states that a בית הכנסת, a house owned by a woman and a house owned by partners all require a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a synagogue, a woman's house and a partners' house are obligated in מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא listing three kinds of houses that need a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds new information. Ownership by a woman or by several people does not remove the obligation, and neither does a building being a בית הכנסת.

keyTerms.meaning: A house owned jointly by partners
A house owned by a woman

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: a synagogue,
a woman's house, and a partners' house
are obligated in mezuza.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּבֵית הָאִשָּׁה וּבֵית הַשּׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new branch about which owners and buildings are obligated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הכנסת, a woman's house and a partners' house are all obligated in מזוזה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to teach something that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the ברייתא, since there seems to be no reason to exempt these houses. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not expected to teach something obvious. So the גמרא looks for the mistake that the ברייתא is coming to prevent.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (so why say it?)

phrases.english: Is it not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא of step 11 needed to be stated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no apparent reason to exempt these houses, so teaching that they are obligated seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One might have read 'your house' as excluding women and partners
steps.stepSummary: The word ״ביתך״ is singular and masculine, so one could have thought it excludes a woman's house and a jointly owned house. The ברייתא teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: ״ביתך״, 'your house', and not her house. ״ביתך״, singular, and not their house. So the ברייתא teaches us that they are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake the ברייתא is coming to prevent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ביתך״ is written in the masculine singular. Read strictly, it could suggest only a house owned by one man. The ברייתא rejects that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / I might have thought

phrases.english: You might say: 'your house' — and not her house,
'your house' — and not their house,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a possible mistaken reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ביתך״ excludes a woman's house and a partners' house.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that they are obligated.

steps.title: Maybe that reading is actually correct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that perhaps women's and partners' houses really are exempt, based on ״ביתך״.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: why not accept the strict reading of ״ביתך״? This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading in step 13 sounded reasonable. So the גמרא demands a reason to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: And say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the dismissal of the הוה אמינא in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a woman's house and a partners' house are obligated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine singular ״ביתך״ could really mean that only one man's house is obligated.

steps.title: The reward of long life applies to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק promises long life for the מצוה of מזוזה. It cannot be that men need long life and women or partners do not, so everyone is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'So that your days may be many, and the days of your children.' Do these people need life, and those do not need life?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from the reward written right after the מצוה that women and partners are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward of long life is tied to the מצוה of מזוזה. Since everyone needs life, everyone shares in the מצוה. This outweighs the strict grammar of ״ביתך״.

keyTerms.meaning: So that your days may be many (the reward for מזוזה)

steps.whatToRemember: A woman's house and a partners' house need a מזוזה, because the reward of long life applies to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: who owns the house does not matter. Every Jewish home needs a מזוזה.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'So that your days may be many, and the days of your children,'
do these need life
and those do not need life?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם וִימֵי בְנֵיכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק (the reward attached to the מצוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ביתך″ limits the obligation to one man's house.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reward of long life applies to all, so women and partners are obligated.

steps.title: So what does the word 'your house' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has just ruled that every house needs a מזוזה. So it asks what the word ״ביתך״ comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the word ״ביתך״, 'your house'?
steps.whatsHappening: Since ״ביתך״ does not limit who must put up a מזוזה, the גמרא asks what that word is there for. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the גמרא rejected the idea that ״ביתך״ excludes women and partners. But the גמרא assumes every word in the תורה teaches something. So it now needs a new job for this word.

keyTerms.meaning: Your house (from the פסוק of מזוזה)

phrases.english: Rather, why do I need 'your house'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion of step 15: if ״ביתך״ does not exclude anyone, what does it teach?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word ״ביתך״ teaches, if it does not limit who is obligated.

steps.title: Following רבא: the מזוזה goes on the side you enter
steps.stepSummary: Following רבא, ״ביתך״ is read as 'the way you come in'. A person steps first with his right foot, so the מזוזה goes on the right side of the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבא, who said: read it as 'the way of your entering'. When a person starts to walk, he lifts his right foot first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבא's teaching. ״ביתך״ tells us where the מזוזה goes, not who must put one up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads ״ביתך״ (beisecha) as if it said ״ביאתך״ (bi'ascha), 'your entering'. So the מזוזה goes on the side you enter from. People naturally step forward with the right foot first, so that side is the right side.
steps.whatToRemember: ״ביתך״ does not exclude women or partners. It teaches that the מזוזה is placed on the right side as you enter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that a מזוזה is put on the right side of the doorway as you walk in.

phrases.english: Like Rava, for Rava said:
The way of your entering,
and when a person lifts (his foot) —
he lifts his right foot first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by giving ״ביתך״ a new job.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״ביתך״ means 'your entering' and places the מזוזה on the right side of the doorway.

steps.title: New ברייתא: these houses become impure with house-leprosy
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that a בית הכנסת, a partners' house and a woman's house can become impure with נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: a בית הכנסת, a house of partners and a woman's house become impure with נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same three kinds of houses. This time the topic is the impurity of נגעי בתים, not מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list matches the מזוזה ברייתא from step 11. The topic switches to the צרעת that can appear on the walls of a house (ויקרא יד). This opens a new branch that will copy the same question-and-answer pattern.

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּבֵית הַשּׁוּתָּפִין וּבֵית הָאִשָּׁה
phrases.english: A synagogue, a partners' house, and a woman's house
become impure with leprous marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא to the one in step 11, now about נגעים instead of מזוזה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הכנסת, a partners' house and a woman's house can all become impure with נגעי בתים.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא. Why would we ever think these houses are different from other houses?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house is a house. Who owns it or what it is used for should not seem to matter. So the ברייתא looks like it is teaching something nobody doubted.

phrases.english: Obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why step 18 needed to be taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be no reason to think these houses would be excluded, so the teaching looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The word 'his' might have excluded women and partners
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״אשר לו הבית״, 'whose house is HIS'. One might think this excludes a woman's house ('hers') and a partners' house ('theirs'). The ברייתא teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: 'And the one whose house is his will come'. 'His', and not hers. 'His', and not theirs. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the possible mistake. Because the word ״לו״ is singular and masculine, we might have excluded women and partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same logic as step 13 with ״ביתך״. ״לו״ means 'to him', which could suggest only one male owner. The ברייתא rejects that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the one whose house it is will come' (ויקרא יד:לה)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
'And the one whose house it is will come,'
'his' — and not hers,
'his' — and not theirs,
so it teaches us (otherwise).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: showing a possible mistake that the ברייתא prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word ״לו״ would exclude a woman's house and a partners' house from נגעים.
steps.terutzMaskana: These houses can also become impure with נגעים.

steps.title: Maybe they really are excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that maybe the reading of ״לו״ is correct, and these houses really are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that it really is so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe ״לו״ really does exclude women and partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as in step 14, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא's ruling beats the simple reading of the פסוק. It now needs a source showing that all houses are included.

keyTerms.meaning: And say it really is so

phrases.english: And say it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling defended in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that women's and partners' houses get נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״לו״ suggests a single male owner, so maybe these houses really are excluded.

steps.title: 'Your possession' is plural, so it includes everyone
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק also says ״אחוזתכם״, 'your (plural) possession'. This shows that all houses are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'In a house of the land of your possession'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from another word in the פסוק that every house can get נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אחוזתכם״ is plural. It speaks to all of כלל ישראל, so it includes houses owned by women and by partners. That overrides the narrow reading of ״לו״.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'In a house of the land of your possession.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from another word in the פסוק

steps.title: So what does the word 'his' teach?
steps.stepSummary: If ״לו″ does not exclude anyone, the גמרא asks why it was written.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the word 'his'?
steps.whatsHappening: Just like with ״ביתך״ in step 16, the גמרא asks what ״לו″ is there for. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לו″ has lost its job as a word that excludes some houses. So the גמרא looks for a different lesson in it.

phrases.english: Rather, why do I need 'his'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 22: if ״לו″ does not exclude anyone, what does it teach?

steps.title: 'His': the stingy man who keeps his house to himself
steps.stepSummary: ״לו״ hints at the cause of נגעים. A person who keeps his things only for himself and lies that he has none to lend is exposed by הקדוש ברוך הוא. When his house gets נגעים, he must empty out all his belongings in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to one who keeps his house only for himself. He does not want to lend his vessels and says he has none. הקדוש ברוך הוא exposes him when he empties out his house. This leaves out someone who lends his vessels to others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that ״לו״ teaches a moral lesson about why נגעים come. It does not teach a legal limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a כהן declares a house impure, its contents are taken out (ויקרא יד:לו). Then everyone sees the things the stingy owner claimed he did not have. A generous person who lends his things does not get this punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: ״לו״ here is NOT a legal limit on which houses can become impure. It describes the type of person whose house gets נגעים, as a punishment.

phrases.english: One who reserves his house for himself,
who does not want to lend his vessels
and says that he does not have (them),
the Holy One, Blessed be He, publicizes him
when he empties his house.
This excludes one who lends his vessels to others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by giving ״לו″ a moral meaning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לו″ points to the stingy owner who keeps his things to himself. His house is struck with נגעים, which exposes his belongings.

steps.title: But another ברייתא says a בית הכנסת does not get leprosy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling about a בית הכנסת. A different ברייתא uses ״לו״ to exclude בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות, because they do not belong to one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a בית הכנסת really become impure with נגעים? But a ברייתא taught: you might think בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות become impure with נגעים. So the פסוק says, 'and the one whose house it is will come'. That means a house that belongs to him. This leaves out houses that do not belong to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one ברייתא against another. One says a בית הכנסת gets נגעים, and the other says it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 included a בית הכנסת. Now a second ברייתא reads ״לו״ as excluding public buildings, which are not owned by one individual. So the two ברייתות seem to contradict each other, and the גמרא will need to resolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: And does a synagogue become impure with leprous marks?
But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יִהְיוּ בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת
phrases.english: One might think that synagogues and study halls
become impure with leprous marks,
therefore the verse states:
'And the one whose house it is will come' —
(a house) that is designated for him,
excluding those that are not designated for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת מִי מִטַּמֵּא בִּנְגָעִים? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ruling in step 18 and challenges it from a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 18 that a בית הכנסת becomes impure with נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא learns from ״לו″ that public buildings like בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות are excluded from נגעים.

steps.title: The two ברייתות follow different Tannaim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is no real contradiction. The ברייתא that makes a בית הכנסת impure follows רבי מאיר, and the ברייתא that exempts it follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and that ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 25. Each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות can disagree when they reflect two sides of a known argument. The ברייתא that says a בית הכנסת can get נגעים follows רבי מאיר. The ברייתא that uses ״לו״ to exclude it follows רבנן. The גמרא proves this argument exists in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer.
This one ... that one. It points to the two sources being compared.
The Rabbis, meaning the majority of Sages

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one follows Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says a synagogue can get נגעים.

phrases.english: that one follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that uses ״לו״ to exclude synagogues.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא — רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to give one single ruling, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Proof that רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about a בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about מזוזה shows that רבי מאיר treats a בית הכנסת without a living space as a home, while חכמים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A בית הכנסת that has a living space for the חזן must have a מזוזה. If it has no living space, רבי מאיר says it must have a מזוזה, and חכמים say it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that רבי מאיר and חכמים really do argue about whether a בית הכנסת counts as a home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a בית הכנסת with a living space needs a מזוזה, because someone lives there. When there is no living space, רבי מאיר still treats it as a home, but חכמים do not. The same view carries over to נגעים: for רבי מאיר it can become impure, and for חכמים it cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא. This introduces a supporting source.
The parchment scroll attached to the doorpost of a home

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about מזוזה, not נגעים. The גמרא uses it because the same question, whether a בית הכנסת counts as a home, decides both laws.

phrases.english: As it was taught: A synagogue

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית דִּירָה לְחַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת —
phrases.english: that has in it a living space for the synagogue attendant
is obligated in mezuza,
and one that has no living space:
Rabbi Meir obligates it,
and the Sages exempt it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the argument claimed in Step 26
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and רבנן argue about whether a בית הכנסת has the status of a home
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about whether a בית הכנסת needs a מזוזה

steps.title: Both ברייתות follow רבנן, but discuss different buildings
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: both ברייתות follow רבנן. One speaks of a בית הכנסת with a living space, and the other of one without.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both follow the רבנן, and there is no difficulty. This one speaks of a בית הכנסת that has a living space, and that one speaks of a בית הכנסת that has no living space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same contradiction. This time it does not need two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even חכמים agree that a בית הכנסת with a living space acts like a home. So it can get נגעים, just as it needs a מזוזה. The ברייתא that excludes synagogues using ״לו״ is speaking about one with no living space.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say. This introduces another possible answer.
Both this one and that one
That does not have in it

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
both this and that follow the Rabbis,
and it is not difficult:
this one is where it has a living space,
that one is where it has no living space.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction in Step 25, instead of the answer in Step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות might seem to need two different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבנן. The difference depends on whether the building has a living space.

steps.title: A third answer: both speak of a בית הכנסת without a living space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a third answer. Both ברייתות speak of a בית הכנסת with no living space, and the difference between them comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both this one and that one speak of a בית הכנסת that has no living space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a third answer. It first says both ברייתות discuss the same kind of building, and explains the difference on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer drops the living-space difference used in Step 28. Both cases have no living space, so the reason they are treated differently must be something else. The גמרא reveals that reason in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say. Here it introduces a third answer.

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished. Wait for the next passage to see what difference the גמרא gives between the two ברייתות.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא וְהָא דְּלֵית בָּהּ בֵּית דִּירָה,
phrases.english: both this and that are where it has no living space,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא דְּלֵית בָּהּ בֵּית דִּירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a third answer to Step 25 and sets aside the living-space split from Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into different cases (incomplete; continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the ברייתות seemed to be whether there is a living space.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases have no living space. A different factor, explained on the next amud, separates them.
